nm_thumb_the.blurb: A twin-summited granite formation tucked into upper La Cueva Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains above Albuquerque. It is a traditional-climbing spot: of ten listed climbs, eight are trad, with one sport route and one scramble. Grades run from fourth class up to 5.12, but most of the routes sit between 5.6 and 5.10, so there is plenty for a solid mid-grade leader. Several lines are multipitch and ridge-like, with real exposure and a scrambling finish, which makes for a committing day rather than a quick lap. Expect a canyon setting reached on foot along the La Luz Trail, with views over the Rio Grande valley. The face catches morning light, so the afternoon is cooler.
nm_thumb_the.approach: Walk down the La Luz Trail past a run of switchbacks and talus slopes until a faint path leaves the trail heading west through the trees. Follow it to the foot of the formation.
